blockingIssues: Conceptual Error in Formula Register and Worked Example 2: The draft teaches the 'spin-only' magnetic moment formula (μ = √(n(n+2))) for lanthanoids and applies it to Ce3+ to get 1.73 BM. In f-block elements, the orbital contribution to the magnetic moment is not quenched, so the spin-only formula is largely invalid (except for f7 configurations). The magnetic moment must be calculated using total angular momentum J (μ = g√(J(J+1))). The actual experimental magnetic moment of Ce3+ is ~2.54 BM. This contradicts standard chemistry curricula like NCERT.

review.reviewNotes: The content generally offers a good summary of lanthanoids, their electronic configurations, and lanthanoid contraction. However, applying the spin-only magnetic moment formula to lanthanoids is a major conceptual inaccuracy for f-block elements and must be revised or heavily contextualized. Please also fix the typographical errors in the self-check section.
